en.headline: Hand-painted lanterns continue at Wan Chai Blue House until Wednesday
en.dek: More than 700 lanterns painted by residents and local illustrators light up the historic Blue House cluster and nearby streets each evening until 14 October.
body: The Mid-Autumn lantern display at the Blue House in Wan Chai remains in place until Wednesday, with the lights switched on from 6pm to 9.30pm each evening.

Organisers said more than 700 hand-painted lanterns, created by residents, members of the public, pet owners and about 50 local illustrators, are hung around the Grade I historic building. The display stretches along Stone Nullah Lane and nearby streets including Kat On Street, Hing Wan Street, King Sing Street and Queen’s Road East.
Admission is free. The lanterns form part of the Blue House’s community programme marking a decade since the cluster’s revitalisation. The display is due to end on 14 October.

zh.headline: 灣仔藍屋手繪花燈展延至周三 每晚亮燈
zh.dek: 超過700盞由街坊及本地插畫家手繪的花燈，每晚6時至9時半點亮藍屋建築群及附近街道，展期至10月14日。
body: 灣仔藍屋的中秋花燈展將持續至周三，每晚6時至9時半亮燈。
主辦單位表示，超過700盞手繪花燈由街坊、公眾、寵物主人及約50位本地插畫家共同創作，懸掛在一級歷史建築藍屋建築群周圍。燈海延伸至石水渠街及附近的吉安街、慶雲街、景星街和皇后大道東。
入場免費。花燈展是藍屋活化十周年社區活動的一部分，將於10月14日結束。
